Item numbers were deliberately preserved through the revision because other guidelines point at them - identifiers must be stable when other things reference them
quote: Moreover, because other reporting guidelines augmenting the checklist refer to item numbers, we kept the existing items under their previous item numbers except for some renumbering of items 2 to 5.

value: Items are admitted or dropped on empirical evidence about whether the practice affects bias, not on what seems desirable
quote: Other items may seem desirable, such as reporting on whether on-site monitoring was done, but a lack of empirical evidence or any consensus on their value cautions against inclusion at this point.

value: Breaking composite items into sub-items closes a loophole in how the checklist is used: an author could cite one page for an item and have addressed only half of it
quote: CONSORT 2010 relieves obfuscations and forces authors to provide page numbers in the checklist for both eligibility and settings.

value: A misused term was replaced by a description of the thing it was supposed to denote, rather than being redefined
quote: We replaced mention of “intention to treat” analysis, a widely misused term, by a more explicit request for information about retaining participants in their original assigned groups [26] .

value: The standard governs content and explicitly not form, because a rigid format was tried and failed
quote: Indeed, SORT [19] tried a rigid format, and it failed in a pilot run with an editor and authors.

value: An ongoing database of methodological studies supplies the evidence for each revision, so the guideline updates from accumulating research rather than from opinion

The CONSORT 2010 Statement is this paper including the 25 item checklist in the table ( Table 1 ) and the flow diagram ( Figure 1 ).
Thirty one members of the CONSORT 2010 Group met in Montebello, Canada, in January 2007 to update the 2001 CONSORT statement.
More than 700 studies comprise the CONSORT database (located on the CONSORT website), which provides the empirical evidence to underpin the CONSORT initiative.
More than 400 journals, published around the world and in many languages, have explicitly supported the CONSORT statement.
After seven major iterations, a revised checklist was distributed to the larger group for feedback.
CONSORT 2010 focuses predominantly on the two group, parallel randomised controlled trial, which accounts for over half of trials in the literature.
